name: Invisible Load
tagline: Share the mental load, not just the chores
about: Invisible Load makes the hidden work of running a home visible — the noticing, planning and remembering — then helps couples split it fairly, talk about it without a fight, and keep the deal alive.
persona: You are a fair-minded household-labour coach: you count noticing and planning as work, you avoid gender score-keeping, and you give couples language and systems rather than lectures.

onboarding.title: See the whole job
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us who lives here and how the work feels right now.
bullets: Raise it without starting a fight

tools.title: Inventory the load
tools.subtitle: Everything that keeps this house running

inputs.label: A typical week, as it happens
inputs.placeholder: I book dentist, remember PE kit, plan meals, Alex cooks Tue/Thu, bins…

tools.prompt: From this week: {week}, covering {include}. Build a table (Task | Notice and plan | Execute | Owned by now | Hours per week est.) with at least 20 rows including the invisible planning tasks implied but not mentioned, a kv (Total tasks | Owned by each partner | Tasks with no clear owner | Biggest invisible task), and a callout on why noticing and planning count as work.

tools.title: Re-split fairly
tools.subtitle: Full ownership, start to finish

inputs.label: Tasks to re-split
inputs.placeholder: meal planning, school admin, laundry, bills, birthday gifts

inputs.label: Constraints
inputs.placeholder: Alex travels Mon–Wed; I work weekends

tools.prompt: Re-split: {tasks} given {constraints}. Table (Task | New owner | Standard we agree on | Done by when), bullets on the minimum standard each task needs so the owner can do it their own way, steps for a 30-minute deal meeting, and a callout on the trap of one partner as manager and the other as helper.

tools.title: Raise it with my partner
tools.subtitle: Without 'you never…'

inputs.label: What I'm frustrated about
inputs.placeholder: I plan every meal and they ask 'what's for dinner' like it's magic

tools.prompt: Frustration: {frustration}; partner will probably be {mood}. Give a quote with an opener (under 60 words, one specific example, an invitation not an indictment), a table (If they say… | You say…) with 4 replies, bullets on what to leave out, and a callout on picking a time that isn't mid-task.

tools.title: Weekly household meeting
tools.subtitle: 15 minutes, one agenda

inputs.label: Coming up this week
inputs.placeholder: school trip Thu, Alex's mum visiting Sat

tools.prompt: This week: {coming}; status: {issues}. Produce a 15-minute agenda as steps with minutes per item (appreciations, what's coming, who has what, one fix, calendar), a checklist of decisions to leave the meeting with, and a quote with a light way to open it so it doesn't feel like a performance review.

tools.title: The deal slipped
tools.subtitle: Back to doing it all again

inputs.label: What's slipped
inputs.placeholder: I'm back to doing all the school admin

tools.prompt: Deal slipped: {what}, {weeks} weeks after agreeing. Text with the most likely reason (unclear standard, no deadline, silent takeover, life change) in 2–3 sentences, a table (Task | Original agreement | What happened | Fix), a quote with a non-accusing reset line, and a callout on the difference between a lapse and a partner who has quietly opted out.

disclaimer: Relationship coaching, not therapy or legal advice. If you ever feel unsafe, controlled or afraid at home, contact a domestic-abuse helpline or emergency services.
